items.title: Testing an ATS-friendly resume template in LibreOffice Writer: tab stops, styles and the PDF text layer
items.pt:
Dot leaders are one setting in Writer's Tabs dialog: the row of dots that runs from a job title across to its dates. On this one-page resume, the open-source OpenResume parser went from 38 correct fields to 22 after I added dot leaders. The page looked fine. The dots were in the PDF's text, so the parser read the company, the dots and the city as one long company name.

I started from a Classic ATS-friendly resume template for Writer, with US Letter and A4 downloads, changed one thing at a time

items.title: Your first 90 days as a team lead: listen, win small, then lead
items.pt:
Picture this: on Friday you merged your last pull request as a developer. On Monday you walk into the team room as the new team lead, and seven people look at you, waiting for some kind of direction. Nobody gives you a README for that moment. In my view, it is one of the hardest role changes in our industry, and what helps most is surprisingly unglamorous: a simple plan for the first three months.

I wrote a detailed guide with question lists and a copyable template in my article 90-day plan for

items.title: Your dashboard shows everything except who is about to quit. Don't build a model to guess it
items.pt:
It is a tempting feature request: "We already have all the CRM and ERP activity. Can we flag the people who are about to leave?" Logins dropping, fewer updates, slower replies. It sounds reasonable. I think it is one of the worst things you can build on top of business data, and there is a more useful thing to build instead.

Some context. I posted a list in Spanish on LinkedIn and expanded it on EGA Futura Discover: ten signs that it is time to leave your job. Stopped learning, a toxic atmosphe

items.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
items.pt: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values

items.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
items.pt: Vision-language models (VLMs) integrate visual and textual information, but their outputs do not reveal internal concept representations. Global workspace theory (GWT) proposes that information is selected from parallel brain processes, integrated in a shared workspace, and made available to specialised processes. items.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
items.pt: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. We present Verify the Verifier, to our knowledge the first framework whose LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker examines a passing regression's traces against the specification. Of 564 bugs inserted into four OpenTitan IPs, 68 are candidate scoreboard

items.title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs
items.pt: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. We thus introduce EditSafetyBench, a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness of advanced image editing systems, containing 5,940 image-instruction
